title: fix(desktop): start the region countdown's clock once the 3 is on screen
body:
## Problem

When a recording started on a region, the countdown read as "3.2...1" instead of "3..2..1". The region case covers a Frame recording and a Screen recording on a single display. The 3 flashed and was almost immediately replaced by the 2.

## Root cause

The recorder's clock and the window that draws the number are separate, and nothing synchronized them.

- The clock is the 1-second `setInterval` in `recorder-store.ts`, which runs in the main window. It started as soon as the recorder reported "3".
- Main creates the recording shade window when it receives that first report (`recording-hub.ts`, `shade.show`). The window becomes visible only on `ready-to-show`, after it has loaded the renderer bundle.
- The 3 was therefore on screen only for whatever part of the first second remained after the load.

The countdown used to live on the visible Record page, so it never waited for a window to load. Record modes moved it onto the shade.

## Fix

- New invoke channel `recording:countdown-visible`. Main resolves it once the shade has shown the first tick, which is the shade's `onShown`. It resolves immediately when there is no region, because the Record page's own countdown is already visible. It also resolves when the region is cleared or abandoned.
- `requestStartRecording` waits for that answer before it starts the interval. The wait is capped at 1.5 s, so a recording never depends on the shade. A cancellation during the wait stays cancelled, guarded by a request token.

## Verification

- Hub tests check that the answer waits for the shade's `onShown`, comes at once without a region, and is released on abandon.
- Store tests check that the 3 is held until the countdown is visible, that the 1.5 s cap applies, and that a cancellation during the wait never starts the engine. The store tests fail on the previous `recorder-store.ts`.
- `check-types` is clean, lint is clean, and the full suite passes (281 files, 2578 tests).

**Not verified:** I did not run a real recording. To check it on the MacBook, use Record → Screen → Start recording. The count should read as an even 3, 2, 1, and Esc during the 3 should still cancel.

This is the first fix of the record start/stop audit. The cancel-hang and performance findings will come in separate PRs.
